title: Luyện Đọc VSTEP: The Rise of Plant-Based Diets (VstepR3-Test 7 (01-04-2026))

tasks.instructions: Directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.

passage.title: The Rise of Plant-Based Diets
passage.text:
In recent years, plant-based diets have shifted from a niche lifestyle choice to a mainstream phenomenon driven by converging concerns about health, environmental sustainability, and animal welfare. Vegetarian and vegan diets — once considered fringe — are now embraced by a growing segment of the population in developed nations, and a wider trend toward flexitarianism (reducing but not eliminating meat consumption) has gained significant traction among people reluctant to make a complete dietary change.

The health case for reducing animal product consumption is supported by substantial research. Studies have linked diets high in red and processed meat to increased risks of colorectal cancer, cardiovascular disease, and type 2 diabetes. Plant-based diets, when properly planned, provide adequate protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals while reducing saturated fat intake. Major health organizations, including the World Health Organization and the American Heart Association, recommend reducing consumption of processed meat and increasing the proportion of plant foods in daily meals.

The environmental argument is equally compelling. Animal agriculture accounts for approximately 14.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions, consumes enormous quantities of water and land, and is a leading driver of deforestation and biodiversity loss. Research published in the journal Science found that shifting to a plant-rich diet is one of the single most effective actions an individual can take to reduce their personal carbon footprint — potentially cutting food-related emissions by more than 50%. As climate awareness grows, many consumers are making dietary choices with environmental consequences explicitly in mind.
